root_idea.summary: The root centers on going beyond or crossing what should remain bounded, with extensions to rapid movement, hostile opposition, wrongful aggression, and separation or distance.
root_idea.development: The semantic development proceeds from transition and exceeding a limit to running, transgression, enmity, aggression, and related notions of distance, interruption, and transmission from one thing to another.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural active participle is presented under its singular citation form عَادِيَةٌ.
The plural active participle is grouped with the corresponding singular citation form مُعْتَدٍ.

senses.definition: To pass beyond, exceed, or transgress a limit.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran this Form I verb describes exceeding what should be observed or passing beyond a proper boundary; grammatical person and aspect vary by occurrence.

senses.definition: To treat as an enemy; to oppose with enmity or hostility.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is a perfect Form III verb describing a former state of hostility that may be changed into reconciliation.

senses.definition: To transgress or pass beyond a prescribed limit.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic Form V construction takes divine laws, commands, or boundaries as what is exceeded.

senses.definition: To commit aggression or transgress a protected limit.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the use of اعتدى as aggression initiated against another or as wrongful exceeding of a rule, right, or boundary.

senses.definition: To respond to an aggressor with a corresponding counteraction.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic retaliatory construction, the wording uses the same lexical root for a response proportionate to an earlier aggression; the context distinguishes requital from initiating wrongdoing.

senses.definition: One who transgresses, acts wrongfully, or exceeds the permitted limit.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic active participle includes a person who exceeds the limit of necessity or otherwise acts beyond what is right; its plural form is عَادُونَ.

senses.definition: A runner or charger; in the Quran, the charging racers, understood as horses making a swift hostile or predatory incursion.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quranic form is the feminine plural عَادِيَاتِ in an oath; the singular citation form is عَادِيَةٌ.
The noun denotes the condition or relationship of hostile opposition, whether arising between individuals, communities, or religious groups.

senses.definition: Aggressive or transgressive action; enmity expressed in conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun is used adverbially for hostile or wrongful conduct, including conduct that causes others to revile what is sacred.
This use presents hostility as directed opposition or enmity; عَدُوّ can function as a noun or adjective and is used for singular, plural, masculine, and feminine referents.

senses.definition: A person or thing that is harmful or hostile in effect, even without deliberately intending hostility.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic discussion includes cases where a relationship or conduct causes harm and therefore warrants caution, although the harmful party need not have consciously chosen enmity.

senses.definition: Wrongful aggression, injustice, or transgressive conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: This use denotes prohibited aggression initiated against another or conduct that exceeds a right or proper limit.

senses.definition: Counteraction against an aggressor in response to the aggression committed.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression excluding aggression except against wrongdoers, the term can refer to a justified response directed at one who has initiated wrongdoing; the surrounding context supplies the limitation.

senses.definition: A side or bank of a valley.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran contrasts the nearer and farther sides of the valley; the form is also used for a lateral part or side generally.

senses.definition: One who transgresses, violates a limit, or commits aggression.
senses.usage_conditions: This active participle is used substantivally and adjectivally; the supplied Quranic forms include both singular and plural inflections.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass from one thing or affair to another; to leave it or turn away from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be omitted when the construction means to turn away from the matter at hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act corruptly, injuriously, or wrongfully toward someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical construction with عَلَى and is kept distinct from the Quranic Form I occurrences whose supplied contexts express passing beyond or transgression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To steal goods or seize what is behind someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage applied to a thief or to the act of taking property by stealth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leap upon someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a physical attack or pounce, not merely verbal or legal transgression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run or move rapidly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe a person or horse and ranges from a swift pace to strenuous running; the related statement that water runs belongs to the same motion branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divert, turn away, or occupy someone so as to prevent attention to an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is عَدَاهُ عَنِ الأَمْرِ or an equivalent expression with the thing from which one is diverted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For evil or mischief to reach someone from another source.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase عَدَانِي مِنْهُ شَرٌّ presents the evil as reaching or befalling the affected person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hate or detest someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct stative usage of the root and is not the Form III verb of treating someone with enmity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To except or exclude, equivalent to “except.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With ما or without it, the following noun may be governed as an object or, in particle-like use, in the genitive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone or something to pass from one matter to another, or to make it pass through and beyond.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related grammatical term تَعْدِيَةُ الفعل describes making a verb transitive, but that grammatical label is not itself treated as a separate lexical meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make distant, withdraw from, or remain aloof from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This construction is distinct from عَادَىَهُ in the sense of treating a person with enmity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take from, raise, neglect, or repeatedly wash the hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The alternatives describe particular treatment of hair during washing or grooming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fold a pillow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized household usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lower one of the supports beneath a cooking pot so that the pot inclines toward the fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is one of the stones supporting the pot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act successively upon two targets, overtaking or striking one immediately after the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is applied to a horse, hunter, or other agent dealing with two quarry animals in one run; it can also describe thrusting two men successively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie or compete with another in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction denotes competition in speed or running ability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a disease, disposition, or harmful condition to pass to another; to infect or transmit it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted condition may be mange, scab, another disease, an evil disposition, or mischief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, strengthen, or avenge someone against a wrongdoer; in judicial use, to hear an accusation and summon the adversary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is someone seeking support or redress against another who has wronged him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a person or horse run or go at a running pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative Form IV construction may mean either making or directing the subject to run.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find food or pasture sufficient to dispense with other provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Classical expressions refer to finding flesh, milk, or pasture so that wine or purchased fodder is unnecessary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or receive a woman’s dowry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction with the dowry as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people or animals to become affected by one another’s disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes reciprocal or successive transmission of a disease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people or animals to die one after another or in large numbers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage may describe successive deaths within a period or widespread death among camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a group to arrive successively with aid or assistance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes successive members of a party coming to support someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people to treat one another with enmity or hostility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This reciprocal Form VI meaning is distinct from the one-sided Form III verb عَادَىَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a matter between parties to become corrupt, complicated, or disputed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is the affair or relationship between the parties rather than the parties themselves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become uneven or dissimilar in its parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage applies to a place whose parts differ in level or character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become distant, remote, or aloof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is used with عن and may describe people, things, or places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In supplication, exceeding the limits of the transmitted rule or customary form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical specialization of the verbal noun and does not replace the Quranic meanings of the finite verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek aid, strengthening, or vengeance from a ruler, governor, commander, or judge against a wrongdoer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is a legal or administrative demand for assistance or redress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To provide aid or assistance against a wrongdoer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This less common direction of the verbal noun describes the assistance itself rather than the request for it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Openly or publicly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning occurs in the fixed expression فَعَلَ كَذَا عَدْوًا بَدْوًا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The broad stones covering a grave or the thin stone used to cover or conceal something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A related usage denotes a piece of wood placed between two other pieces; the reported senses concern covering or separating materials.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People who are distant, strangers, foreigners, or unrelated by kinship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a plural lexical use associated with عَدُوّ, not the ordinary Quranic noun meaning an enemy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vigorous run or a stretch of running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This feminine verbal noun is used for a vehement run of the kind called عَدْو.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extent of eyesight or a distance comparable to a bowshot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may indicate the distance separating one person or thing from another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An elevated place or the lateral part of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This branch is distinct from the Quranic sense of a valley side as a geographical location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place extending far or broadly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Classical spatial usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sweet kind of plant or herbage called خُلَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This botanical sense is distinct from the geographical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: According to a reported usage, a stone covering a grave or well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence attributes this rare sense to some authorities and leaves the lexical form and plural partly uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remote or distant affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression أُمُورٌ عِدْوَةٌ or a closely related construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The transmission of mange, scab, or another disease from one person or animal to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term also appears in the negated expression لا عَدْوَى, denying autonomous causal transmission in the cited traditional formulation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Badness, corruption, unsoundness, or a harmful condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct nominal use from disease transmission.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A demand made to a governor or judge for aid, retribution, or the summoning of an adversary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also denote the aid requested or the sealed token used to summon the person whose presence is required.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distance, remoteness, or prolonged separation, especially between dwellings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may describe a long-standing state of separation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An occupation, hindrance, or business that diverts someone from another matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural عَوَادِي can denote intervening accidents or obstacles of time and fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The shifting or varying of time or fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of interruption and changing circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A severely distressing or afflicting form of yearning or longing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense describes the effect of intense desire on its sufferer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An uneven or uncomfortable mount, saddle, seat, or place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term describes something on which the rider or sitter cannot remain at ease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry, hard, rough, or uneven ground, including a hard stratum in a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description includes land that is difficult to walk or ride over and from which a digger turns aside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A brief or slight making of a camel to kneel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage associated with mounting or dismounting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to camels pasturing on the herbage called عُدْوَة or on حَمْض.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Authorities differ over whether the designation refers to grazing on حَمْض or remaining among عِضَاه trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Summer herbage appearing after the departure of spring growth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to young trees that become green and are grazed by camels, or to the plants called رَبْل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Young sheep or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate animal-naming usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Female infants up to about forty days old, according to one reported usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records disagreement about this form and its relation to similarly pronounced words; the designation reportedly ends after the infant’s hair is cut.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Predatory or aggressively attacking, especially of a wolf or other beast of prey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is explained by the animal’s attacking people and making them prey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Running vehemently or frequently; possessing great running speed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a horse and, by extension, to a man or other runner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single run or uninterrupted heat to a goal or limit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is especially applied to a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The tract coextensive with something in breadth and length.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One may keep to the tract alongside a road, river, or mountain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seizing or carrying off by force, or snatching unexpectedly; by extension, a predatory lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal epithet is motivated by the lion’s injurious seizure of people as prey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wrongdoing, injury, evil, or mischief; also sharpness of temper or anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: As a substantive, the feminine form can denote harmful conduct or its effects rather than an active runner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The harm or hurt caused by poison.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative extension of injurious effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Grapevines planted at the feet or roots of large trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is explained as deriving from عَادِيَةٌ in this botanical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More transmissible or contagious than something else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in comparative expressions about mange, scab, yawning, or similar transmission.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More wrongful, hostile, or vehement in running than another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The comparative may select among the root’s branches according to context, including aggression and speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Most effective in aiding or avenging someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An irregular comparative formation associated with the causative sense of aiding a wronged person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An uneven place whose parts differ in level or character.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is used of ground containing burrows, trenches, or other irregularities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way beyond or an alternative course; in the fixed phrase, no possibility of passing from one person to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression مَا لِي عَنْ فُلَانٍ مَعْدًى means that one cannot leave or bypass that person for another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Treated wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction مَعْدِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ describes the person against whom wrongdoing has been committed.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Grammatical terminology, not an independent lexical branch.
Unexplained poetic plural; no independent meaning is supplied.
Editorial report of an apparent mistranscription.
Relative adjective from a different root, with no independent meaning for this root.

cautions: The form عَادِيَاتِ in 100:1 is presented under عَادِيَةٌ as its singular active-participle citation form; its Quranic sense is the racer or charger, not the separate Classical substantive meaning of wrongdoing.
عَدُوّ can function as both noun and adjective and is not restricted to a single grammatical number or gender.
عُدْوَان and اِعْتِدَاء may describe either initiated aggression or a proportionate response, depending on the Quranic construction and context.
The rare Classical senses associated with عِدْوَةٌ, عَدَوِيَّةٌ, and related forms include attributed or disputed lexical reports and are kept outside the Quranic senses.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The reported stone-covering sense under عِدْوَةٌ is attributed to some authorities and its exact form and plural are uncertain; it is retained as a qualified Classical meaning rather than assigned to a Quranic sense.
Lane's historical Quran citation in the discussion of عَدَا is not converted into a modern verse location; modern Quran examples here use only secure QAC locations.
